children: "Gold is a good servant but a bad master".

This Italian saying offers a simple warning about wealth and the power it can have over our lives. Money can make life easier. But when the pursuit of wealth becomes the main purpose of life, it can also control our decisions, priorities and relationships.

The proverb suggests that money is useful when we remain in control of it. We can use wealth to meet our needs, support our families and create opportunities. It can provide security and freedom when managed wisely.

However, problems begin when money becomes the thing controlling our choices. A person may start measuring success only through income, possessions or social status. Over time, the desire for more can become difficult to satisfy.
When does money become the master?

Money becomes a “master” when it dictates how we live. Someone might work constantly despite having enough because they fear losing their wealth. Another person may sacrifice friendships, family time or personal happiness to earn more.
The proverb reminds us that financial success should serve our lives rather than replace them.
Why is this lesson still relevant?

Modern life often connects success with material possessions. Social media can make this pressure even stronger. People constantly see expensive homes, luxury holidays, designer clothes and seemingly perfect lifestyles.
This can create the feeling that having more means being happier or more successful. But wealth cannot guarantee meaningful relationships, peace of mind or a sense of purpose.
What can we learn from it?

The proverb does not suggest that money is bad. Instead, it encourages us to understand its proper place in life. Money is a tool. It can help us build a secure future and achieve important goals. But it should not become the measure of our entire existence.

title: Italian Proverb of the Day: "Gold is a good servant but a bad master" - A timeless lesson about money, wealth and control
